[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
delete_http_settings removes an Application Gateway HTTP setting that can reference a probe; it should be ordered before delete_probe so the probe is not removed while still in use. Add an explicit dependency from delete_http_settings to delete_probe.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
HTTP settings can reference probes, so the HTTP-settings delete action should run before the probe delete action. Make the HTTP-settings deletion node depend on the probe deletion node so Terraform destroys the settings first.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
HTTP settings can reference probes, so their deletion must complete before the probe is deleted. Add the dependency in this direction; a dependency from probe deletion to HTTP-settings deletion would reverse the required destroy order.

----------------------------------------

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
delete_http_settings references a probe (HTTPSETTINGS is associated with a PROBE), so the HTTP settings must be destroyed before the probe. But delete_http_settings only depends on set_probe (the create-time resource), not delete_probe, so destroy order between delete_http_settings and delete_probe is undefined and the probe may be deleted while still referenced. The destroy-time dependency should be on delete_probe.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
`null_resource.delete_http_settings` runs a destroy-time local-exec that deletes the backend HTTP settings, which reference health probes. In Azure Application Gateway a probe cannot be removed while an HTTP setting still references it, so during teardown the HTTP settings must be deleted first. The resource's `depends_on` lists `null_resource.set_probe` (a create-time resource that does nothing on destroy) instead of `null_resource.delete_probe`, so no destroy ordering is established and the probe may be deleted before the settings that reference it (its `on_failure = fail` would then abort the destroy). It should depend on `null_resource.delete_probe`.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
delete_http_settings must run before the probe is removed (HTTP settings reference the probe via enable_probe/probe), but no dependency expresses that: its depends_on lists the create-time set_probe rather than the cleanup resource delete_probe. It should depend on delete_probe so the HTTP-settings cleanup is destroyed before the probe cleanup.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
delete_http_settings has no dependency on delete_probe. HTTP settings are created after probes (set_http_settings depends on set_probe) and can reference a probe, so during destroy the http settings must be removed before the probe. Its depends_on lists set_probe (a create-time resource), which establishes no destroy-time ordering with the probe's delete script; deleting the probe first would fail because it is still referenced.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
delete_http_settings destroys HTTP settings that reference probes, but it has no dependency on delete_probe (it depends on set_probe instead, which has no destroy-time provisioner and imposes no destroy ordering). On destroy, HTTP settings must be deleted before the probes they reference; add delete_probe to delete_http_settings' depends_on.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
delete_frontend_port should be ordered after delete_http_listener cleanup because the listener uses the frontend port; otherwise the port may be removed while the listener still references it. Add an explicit dependency from delete_frontend_port to delete_http_listener.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The frontend port deletion action should wait until HTTP listeners that use the port have been deleted.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
Frontend ports used by HTTP listeners must not be removed until those listeners have been deleted. The frontend-port deletion currently has no ordering dependency on listener deletion.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The probe deletion action should wait until HTTP settings that may reference the probe have been deleted; otherwise Azure may reject or retain the referenced probe.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The probe must be removed only after HTTP settings that may reference it are removed; otherwise deleting the probe can leave the Application Gateway configuration referencing a missing probe. Make the probe deletion depend on the HTTP settings deletion.

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
delete_http_listener is destroyed before delete_http_settings etc., but it has no ordering dependency on delete_frontend_port. A frontend port cannot be removed while an HTTP listener still references it, so on destroy the port could be deleted before the listener, causing the destroy to fail. The destroy-time dependency should be on delete_frontend_port (the create-time set_frontend_port it currently depends on does not establish this ordering).

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
`null_resource.delete_http_listener` deletes the HTTP listeners, which reference the frontend ports. A frontend port cannot be deleted while a listener still uses it, so the listeners must be torn down before the frontend port. The resource's `depends_on` lists `null_resource.set_frontend_port` (a create-only resource whose destroy provisioner does nothing) instead of `null_resource.delete_frontend_port`, so no destroy ordering exists and `delete_frontend_port` may run first, failing on a still-referenced port (`on_failure = fail`). It should depend on `null_resource.delete_frontend_port`.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
The HTTP listener references a frontend port (set_http_listener depends_on set_frontend_port), so on destroy the listener cleanup must happen before the frontend-port cleanup. delete_http_listener instead lists the create-time set_frontend_port, which establishes no destroy ordering; it should depend on delete_frontend_port.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
delete_http_listener has no dependency on delete_frontend_port. Listeners are created after frontend ports and reference them (PORT), so the frontend port must be deleted after all listeners. Its depends_on references set_frontend_port (the create-time resource), not the delete-time resource, so the port's az delete can run before the listener delete and fail because the port is still in use.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
delete_http_listener destroys listeners bound to frontend ports, but it depends on set_frontend_port (a create-phase resource with no destroy provisioner) rather than delete_frontend_port, which has no depends_on and is otherwise unordered. On destroy, listeners must be deleted before the frontend ports they reference; add delete_frontend_port to delete_http_listener's depends_on.
